title: On the Diffusibility of High-Dimensional Latents
why_read: A technically deep paper on an important tradeoff in diffusion model architecture design that matters for state-of-the-art image generation systems.
analysis: This paper studies representation autoencoders used to let diffusion models generate images in a compressed feature space rather than raw pixels, which is a common efficiency trick in modern generative models. It finds that fine-tuning encoders for better reconstruction quality inadvertently shrinks the effective dimensionality of the useful signal, which then hurts the standard velocity-prediction training objective used in flow matching. The proposed fix is switching to predicting the clean data directly rather than the noise-removal direction, which better matches the lower-dimensional signal manifold. This is a genuinely useful and somewhat counterintuitive finding for anyone building or tuning diffusion-based image generators.
